title: Decision: the call announcement carries the room and an ended marker, and nothing else
description:
Mark decided 2026-11-23, completing decision mimid-1wgh.116 (the key's
name and that its value is a map) for bead mimid-1wgh.114.1.

THE QUESTION. The announcement is an ordinary message in the parent chat
whose text any client renders, carrying the private-use extension key
"draft-atwood-mimi-calls/call" that a call-capable client reads. What is
in its map?

CHOSEN: the call room's URI, and a marker a later announcement sets when
the call has ended. Nothing else.

  "draft-atwood-mimi-calls/call": { "room": "mimi://a.example/r/<call>" }

and, for the end:

  "draft-atwood-mimi-calls/call": { "room": "...", "ended": true }

WHY NOT MORE, which was the recommendation and is the thing to keep in
view: who started a call is already the message's sender, and when is
already its timestamp. Repeating either in the map gives a client two
sources for one fact and tempts it to compute liveness from the
message -- "started forty minutes ago, probably over" -- which decision
mimid-1wgh.117 says it must not do, because liveness is not knowable
from the chat.

WHY THE ENDED MARKER IS WORTH IT ANYWAY: without it a chat line stays
ambiguous forever, and the honest alternative was for clients to render
nothing about the end at all. The marker lets the line read "Call
ended". It stays ADVISORY, exactly as decision mimid-1wgh.117 settled: a
sender that crashes never sends it, so its ABSENCE MEANS "NOT KNOWN" and
never "still going". A client that shows a live badge because no ended
marker arrived has made the mistake mimid-1wgh.117 exists to prevent.

THE TENSION, stated rather than smoothed over: an ended marker is the
one field that does invite liveness thinking, and it is in. The
difference is that it is a positive statement someone made ("this call
is over") rather than an inference from a timestamp. Only its presence
means anything.

SHAPE NOTES:
- The map is extensible by design (decision mimid-1wgh.116 chose a map
  over a bare string for this), so a field can be added later without a
  second key.
- "room" is the call room's URI, not a store key: the announcement
  crosses providers, and a store key is local.
- An ended announcement is a new message, not an edit of the first: an
  edit is only the sender's to make, and whoever ends a call need not be
  whoever started it.
notes:
SUPERSEDED by decision mimid-1wgh.128 (Mark, 2026-11-24). The map now carries "room" plus optional "media" and "subject", not "the room's URI and an ended marker, and nothing else".

WHAT CHANGED THE ANSWER, and it is a fact this bead did not have: the receiving side projects a VTCCall from the call room, the room carries neither the media kinds nor the subject, so both are EMPTY on every side but the creator's. Found building bead mimid-1wgh.114.11, after this bead closed. The announcement is the only place either crosses.

WHAT SURVIVES AND STILL BINDS:
  - "ended" stays, advisory, and an ended announcement is a NEW message rather than an edit, since whoever ends a call need not be whoever started it.
  - "room" is the call room's URI, not a store key: the announcement crosses providers and a store key is local.
  - The sender and the time stay OUT of the map: they are already the message's, and two sources for one fact tempt a client to infer liveness, which decision mimid-1wgh.117 forbids. media and subject are descriptive rather than temporal, which is why they do not reopen that risk.
  - The map being extensible was this bead's and mimid-1wgh.116's own reasoning for choosing a map over a string, so adding fields is the mechanism working, not a workaround.

mimid-1wgh.117 is NOT superseded and governs rendering: an invitation, never a live badge.
close_reason: Mark 2026-11-23: the room's URI and an ended marker; sender and time come from the message itself.
